target_customer: Freight forwarders and logistics operators that process large volumes of emailed shipping documents and invoices
problem: Logistics teams re-key data from PDFs, scans and emails (invoices, bookings, bills of lading) into systems such as CargoWise, which is slow and error prone.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for document data extraction and workflow automation, sold to logistics companies
product_category: Logistics document automation (NLP and machine learning)

founders.name: Jenna Brown
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists her as Founder and CEO but gives no background. Secondary pages disagree on her prior employers, so none are recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting structured data from messy, varied logistics documents needed NLP and ML plus integrations into forwarder systems; hard for a small team but built on standard techniques of the period.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with forwarder systems and models trained on many customers' documents raised switching costs, but generic OCR and document AI vendors could approach the same job.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WiseTech Global, maker of the CargoWise forwarder platform that Shipamax integrates with, bought Shipamax in November 2022 and said it would fold the technology into the CargoWise document engine.

market_need_then: Forwarders handle up to many parties and large volumes of unstructured documents per shipment; the YC description frames this as a mountain of manual work. No dated spend figure was found.

branding.domain_note: shipamax.com, an exact .com; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B logistics positioning ('simple, end-to-end automation').

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself, no mascot or community found; the name is distinctive but the brand was a quiet B2B one. After acquisition shipamax.com shows only a 'part of WiseTech Global' redirect page.

outcome_analysis: Shipamax raised a 2.5 million dollar seed in 2017 and a 7 million dollar Series A in January 2020 while selling document automation to logistics firms, with CargoWise integrations a stated reason customers chose it. WiseTech Global, whose platform it integrated with, acquired it in November 2022 and planned to embed the technology in CargoWise. The price was not disclosed, so whether this was a strong or soft exit is unknown.
notes: Seed seen in TechCrunch, tech.eu and UKTN listings (search results); Series A seen in TechCrunch and FreightWaves listings. Some aggregators give $3M seed or $9.5M total; not used. Co-founder names appear on secondary pages but not on the YC page, so only Jenna Brown is listed. No dated 2017 competitor source was found, so the list is empty; current alternatives (Raft, Nabu, Rossum) are later or undated.
